disposition: retain with authority corrections as an optional research-acquisition pack; not universal core

invocation.when: User requests internet research/search/look-up, shares a URL, or names a listed platform.
invocation.boundary: Use only the requested platform and user-approved access scope; a dedicated platform skill takes precedence.
invocation.not_for: Report writing, analysis, translation, posting, commenting, or liking.

execution.recommended: Task-triggered, read-only routing: health-check only explicitly requested login-backed platforms, select the reported backend, read the matching reference, follow its retry chain, and require non-empty content.
execution.alternatives: Use a public web-reader/search route, a dedicated platform skill, or an already configured user-directed provider; report unavailable backends instead of installing or logging in.
execution.authority: Configuration, login, installation, browser sessions, cookie/key import, and possible-cost provider fallback require explicit user authorization.

changes.summary: Make invocation need- and consent-scoped, keep broad research need-driven, make update checks opt-in, and establish explicit authority boundaries with stable question markers.
Clarify that login, credential or browser-session use, dependency installation, system configuration, and GitHub write commands are not authorized by a read-only research skill.
Add the complete source-grounded review, provenance, per-skill execution recommendation, human questions, validation record, and limitations.

questions.question: Should Agent Reach remain an optional internet-research-acquisition pack, or be promoted to universal core?
questions.recommendation: Retain it as optional until provider support, maintenance ownership, licensing permission, and the desired breadth of automatic activation are accepted by a human.
questions.rationale: The tree spans public and login-backed platforms, browser sessions, many external CLIs/MCPs, and provider-specific fallbacks. Installation footprint and upstream collection size do not establish universal need or reliable availability.

questions.question: Should configuration, login, installation, cookie/key import, and browser-session actions require explicit per-action user consent?
questions.recommendation: Yes. Explain credential scope, storage location, data sharing, and possible cost before each such action, and otherwise report the backend as unavailable.
questions.rationale: The original entrypoints said the agent would complete setup after the user supplied cookies or one extension click, while references include package installs, system installs, logins, credential writes, and remote GitHub writes.
